subproblem.title: Off S both ∂(T⌞S) and (∂T)⌞S vanish
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let μ, μ' be measures on ℝ^P, let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) be arbitrary maps, and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let A ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) and B ∈ 𝒟_k(U) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_S ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (Bochner integrals). Then ∂A(θ) = 0 and B(θ) = 0 for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose topological support tsupport θ is disjoint from S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (A : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (B : GeometricCurrentOn U k), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), A ω = ∫ x in S, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, B θ = ∫ x in S, ξ' x ((θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → ∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, Disjoint (tsupport (θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) S → A.boundary θ = 0 ∧ B θ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4 of the parent proof of cmcs_slice_support, with the set {f < t} replaced by an arbitrary set S and η₊ replaced by an arbitrary θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose support misses S. For a form θ write θ̂ for its underlying map ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P). Write dθ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k θ ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U); its underlying form is exteriorDerivative θ̂, and ∂A(θ) = A(dθ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, a definitional equality).
1. (Vanishing on S.) Let x ∈ S.
   (a) Since tsupport θ̂ ∩ S = ∅, x ∉ tsupport θ̂, hence θ̂(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
   (b) Since tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂) ⊆ tsupport θ̂ (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), x ∉ tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂), hence (exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x) = 0.
   (c) ξ(x) and ξ'(x) are linear. Hence ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) = 0 and ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) = 0 for all x ∈ S.
2. (Boundary term.) The representation of A applied to ω := dθ gives
∂A(θ) = A(dθ) = ∫_S ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) dμ(x).
The integrand vanishes at every point of S by step 1, so this integral is 0 by Mathlib setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero (no integrability is needed).
3. (Restricted boundary term.) By the representation of B, B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) dμ'(x). This is 0 by step 1 and setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero.
4. (Conclusion.) ∂A(θ) = 0 and B(θ) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: On S, θ̂ = 0 and exteriorDerivative θ̂ = 0, because S misses tsupport θ̂ ⊇ tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂).
∂A(θ) = A(dθ) = ∫_S ξ(dθ̂) dμ = 0, since the integrand vanishes on S (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(θ̂) dμ' = 0, for the same reason.

audit.reason: The prose matches the exact standalone Lean proposition. Disjointness makes the form and its exterior derivative vanish on S; linearity of each multivector makes both integrands zero there. Applying the two supplied representations and the unconditional zero set-integral lemma proves both conjuncts. The proof is complete, independent of the other children, and non-circular.
